title: Bacillus Endophthalmitis: Fulminant Ocular Infection
summary: Bacillus endophthalmitis is one of the most fulminant and visually devastating ophthalmic emergencies, characterized by rapid intraocular destruction within 12 to 24 hours. Primarily caused by Bacillus cereus following intraocular trauma or foreign bodies, immediate diagnostic sampling, intravitreal antibiotics, and prompt vitrectomy are required to prevent permanent blindness.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Bacillus endophthalmitis is a rapidly progressive, catastrophic intraocular infection caused primarily by Bacillus cereus and Bacillus thuringiensis. Characterized by explosive panophthalmitis, excruciating ocular pain, severe ring-shaped corneal infiltrates, and loss of vision within 12-24 hours, it represents one of the most acute medical and surgical emergencies in clinical ophthalmology.

references.citation: Durand ML. Endophthalmitis. N Engl J Med. 2017;377(1):55-64.
Callegan MC, et al. Bacterial endophthalmitis: therapeutic challenges and host responses. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2002;21(2):189-203.
Essex RW, et al. Post-traumatic endophthalmitis. Ophthalmology. 2004;111(11):2015-2022.

branches: Hemolysin BL: Causes rapid photoreceptor membrane cell lysis
Phospholipase C: Hydrolyzes cellular membrane lipids, generating tissue necrosis
Enterotoxins & Proteases: Trigger explosive intraocular inflammatory degradation
Flagellar Motility: Rapid migration through vitreous humor within hours of inoculation

references.citation: Callegan MC, et al. Pathway of retinal destruction in Bacillus cereus endophthalmitis. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci. 2003;44(10):4390-4397.

rows: Penetrating ocular trauma with soil/organic soil or metallic IOFB
Young males, agricultural or industrial construction workers
Hematogenous seeding from systemic sepsis, catheter, or IV drug use
Rare intraoperative contamination during cataract or vitreoretinal surgery

references.citation: Miller JJ, et al. Endophthalmitis caused by Bacillus species. Am J Ophthalmol. 2008;145(5):883-888.

sections.title: Clinical Manifestations & Cardinal Symptoms
content: Rapid onset of excruciating, unremitting deep ocular pain within 12 to 24 hours post-injury
Profound vision loss rapidly deteriorating to Light Perception (LP) or No Light Perception (NLP)
Severe eyelid edema, intense conjunctival chemosis, and marked proptosis (Panophthalmitis)
Pathognomonic corneal ring infiltrate (Wessely ring) secondary to antigen-antibody complex deposition
Dense hypopyon, rapid vitreous liquefaction, and total loss of red reflex

references.citation: Dave VP, et al. Clinical profile and outcomes of Bacillus endophthalmitis. Semin Ophthalmol. 2018;33(4):550-555.

rows: Immune complex precipitation from bacterial exotoxin antigens
Dense hypopyon, heavy fibrin, elevated IOP
Explosive iridocyclitis and trabecular meshwork outflow obstruction
Bacterial proliferation and enzymatic liquefaction of vitreous
Loss of red reflex, extensive perivascular necrosis
Direct toxins (Hemolysin BL) destroying photoreceptor layers

references.citation: Foster C, et al. Diagnosis and Treatment of Endophthalmitis. AAO Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC). 2022-2023.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Lab Protocols
content: Immediate Vitreous Tap or Anterior Chamber Aspirate prior to antibiotic initiation
Urgent Gram Stain: Demonstrates large, boxcar-shaped Gram-positive spore-forming bacilli
Microbiological Cultures: Inoculate onto Blood Agar, Chocolate Agar, and Thioglycollate Broth
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR): Rapid 16S rRNA gene sequence identification
Orbital CT / B-Scan Sonography: Detect intraocular foreign body (IOFB) and evaluate posterior scleral integrity

references.citation: Jonas JB, et al. Infectious Endophthalmitis: Diagnosis and Treatment Protocols. Ophthalmology. 2018;125(7):1020-1032.

rows: Corneal ring infiltrate, severe pain, proptosis, rapid NLP
Large Gram-positive rods with central/subterminal spores
Mild-to-moderate pain, low-grade vitritis, indolent course
Severe pain, dense fibrinous hypopyon, rapid vitritis
Soupy corneal necrosis, greenish purulent discharge

references.citation: Kanski JJ, Bowling B. Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systemic Approach. 8th ed. Elsevier; 2016.

sections.title: Staging & Disease Progression Timeline
content: Stage 1 (0-12h): Mild AC flare, photophobia, foreign body sensation following ocular trauma
Stage 2 (12-24h): Rapidly rising IOP, dense hypopyon, vitreous haze, early corneal ring infiltrate
Stage 3 (24-48h): Panophthalmitis, severe chemosis, proptosis, total retinal necrosis, drop to NLP
Stage 4 (>48h): Scleral necrosis, phthisis bulbi, or requirement for evisceration / enucleation

references.citation: Callegan MC, et al. Rate of intraocular toxin production in Bacillus endophthalmitis. Infect Immun. 1999;67(1):253-257.

sections.title: Emergency Management Protocol
content: Step 1: Immediate Diagnostic Vitreous Tap / Biopsy to obtain microbiological specimens
Step 2: Intravitreal Injection of Vancomycin (1.0 mg / 0.1 mL) PLUS Ceftazidime (2.25 mg / 0.1 mL)
Step 3: Emergent Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) within hours to physically reduce toxin and bacterial load
Step 4: Surgical Removal of Intraocular Foreign Body (IOFB) via sclerotomy or corneal incision
Step 5: Systemic Antibiosis with Oral Moxifloxacin (400 mg daily) or IV Vancomycin (1g Q12H) + Fortified Topical Vancomycin (50 mg/mL)

references.citation: Relhan N, et al. Endophthalmitis: Management strategies and visual outcomes. Curr Ophthalmol Rep. 2018;6(2):124-131.

sections.title: Surgical Pearls & Intraoperative Strategy
content: Perform early 23G or 25G Pars Plana Vitrectomy to evacuate inflammatory debris and exotoxins
Avoid aggressive posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) induction if retina is necrotic to prevent giant retinal tears
Infusion fluid must NOT contain un titratable antibiotics; rely on direct intravitreal bolus post-vitrectomy
Intravitreal Dexamethasone (400 mcg / 0.1 mL) remains controversial; used selectively after antimicrobial cover to dampen immune-mediated tissue destruction

references.citation: Kuhn F, et al. Complete vitrectomy for traumatic endophthalmitis. Ophthalmology. 2005;112(9):1639-1640.

sections.title: Complications & Visual Prognosis
content: Prognosis is poor: >70% of eyes deteriorate to No Light Perception (NLP) despite emergency treatment
Panophthalmitis requiring surgical Evisceration or Enucleation occurs in up to 30-40% of cases
Combined Tractional and Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment secondary to severe vitreoretinal scarring
Phthisis Bulbi secondary to ciliary body destruction and permanent hypotony

references.citation: Bhagole MD, et al. Visual outcomes in Bacillus cereus endophthalmitis. Retina. 2012;32(8):1612-1617.

sections.title: Red Flag Clinical Warnings
content: History of open globe injury involving soil, farm machinery, or metallic foreign body
Rapid escalation of deep ocular pain and vision loss within 12 hours of trauma
Pathognomonic corneal Wessely ring infiltrate or rapid stromal ring melting
Proptosis, restriction of extraocular movements, and severe chemosis indicative of orbital panophthalmitis extension
Microscopic finding of Gram-positive spore-forming rods on urgent vitreous aspirate

references.citation: Durand ML. Bacterial endophthalmitis. Infect Dis Clin North Am. 2021;35(4):825-843.

content.explanation: B: Blast/Soil Trauma; A: Acute fulminant onset (<24h); C: Corneal ring infiltrate; I: Intravitreal Vancomycin; L: Loss of vision rapid; L: Lysis by exotoxins (Hemolysin BL); U: Urgent vitrectomy; S: Spore-forming rod

references.citation: Ophthalmic Review Board Prep. High-Yield Microbiology in Ophthalmology. 2021.

sections.title: Key Exam & Practice Pearls
content: Bacillus cereus is the single most common pathogen in post-traumatic endophthalmitis with soil-contaminated foreign bodies
Vancomycin and Clindamycin are the intravitreal drugs of choice; Bacillus species are resistant to penicillins and many cephalosporins
The corneal ring infiltrate in Bacillus endophthalmitis represents an immune complex deposition, not direct corneal bacterial infection
Surgical delay beyond 12-24 hours post-trauma significantly increases the rate of total visual loss and evisceration

references.citation: AAO Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC). Section 9: Intraocular Inflammation and Uveitis. 2022-2023.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Evidence & Studies
content: Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study (EVS, 1995): Proved PPV benefits post-cataract endophthalmitis with LP vision; NOTE: EVS guidelines DO NOT apply to post-traumatic or Bacillus endophthalmitis where immediate PPV is required regardless of vision.
Callegan et al. Pathophysiology Series: Proved that Bacillus exotoxins cause irreversible photoreceptor destruction within 12 hours of infection, establishing the ultra-short therapeutic window.
Traumatic Endophthalmitis Clinical Series: Demonstrates that early primary vitrectomy within 24 hours doubles the rate of ocular globe retention compared to systemic/intravitreal antibiotics alone.

references.citation: Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study Group. Results of the Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study. Arch Ophthalmol. 1995;113(12):1479-1496.
Callegan MC, et al. Bacillus endophthalmitis. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2005;24(2):231-253.

sections.title: Special Populations: Pediatric & IVDU Contexts
sections.content: In pediatric penetrating trauma (e.g., non-powder gun or agricultural injury), Bacillus endophthalmitis presents diagnostic challenges due to inability to express pain early. In intravenous drug users (IVDU), endogenous Bacillus cereus endophthalmitis presents with bilateral rapid posterior focal infiltrate and vitritis, requiring emergent bilateral vitrectomy and systemic intravenous vancomycin.

references.citation: Khatib L, et al. Endogenous Bacillus cereus endophthalmitis in IV drug abusers. Retin Cases Brief Rep. 2016;10(2):128-131.
